## Executive summary

This reproduction verifies all 5 major claims of the paper through numerical audits and scaled experiments. The paper provides a unified SDE framework for Distributed Compressed SGD (DCSGD) and Distributed SignSGD (DSignSGD) under (L₀,L₁)-smoothness, showing that (1) DSGD requires adaptive stepsize scaling inversely with gradient norm, (2) compression inflates the effective noise parameter, (3) gradient normalization is a necessary stability condition, (4) DSignSGD converges under heavy-tailed noise without decaying schedules, and (5) these phenomena are empirically observable on MLPs.

All claims were verified using self-contained numerical audits on toy problems (quadratic and quartic objectives) and an MLP regression task. No GPU was needed — all experiments ran on CPU in under 60 seconds total. No official code repository was available for this paper (authors confirm Code: TBD), so all implementations are independent.

## Scope & cost

| | This reproduction | Full replication |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Numerical audits on toy objectives (quartic, quadratic) + MLP regression (20→32→1) | Full-scale experiments on ResNet-18/ViT with CIFAR-10, multi-GPU distributed training |
| Hardware | CPU only | Multi-GPU distributed setup |
| Compute time | < 60 seconds total | Hours to days |
| Cost | $0 | Estimated hundreds of dollars |
| Outcome | All 5 claims supported | Not attempted |
